series_synopsis: In 2010, the world discovered the first digital weapon capable of physical destruction. This is the terrifying story of Stuxnet, a piece of code that silently breached an impenetrable offline bunker to sabotage an entire nation's nuclear program.

full_script.title: The 500KB Code That Destroyed a Nuclear Bunker (Part 1)
full_script.description: How did a computer virus physically destroy steel centrifuges inside an impenetrable underground facility? Discover the shocking true story of Stuxnet, the world's first digital weapon. Subscribe for more dark tech stories!
full_script.narration: Deep underground in the Iranian desert, thousands of steel centrifuges were silently spinning at supersonic speeds inside an airtight nuclear bunker. The facility was completely cut off from the global internet, an impenetrable fortress guarded by concrete blast doors. But then, an innocent-looking metal USB flash drive was intentionally dropped in the facility parking lot. An unsuspecting engineer picked it up, walked inside, and plugged it directly into an offline computer terminal. The malicious code didn't crash the screens; instead, it secretly seized control of the industrial valves, spinning the centrifuges out of control until the metal ripped apart. For months, the physical machines shattered while the control screens falsely displayed that everything was operating normally. Stuxnet proved that software was no longer just digital data, but a physical missile capable of destroying the real world.
